name: World Be Free
label: Revelation
lede: Members of Terror, Strife, Judge and Gorilla Biscuits named a band after a basketball player who changed his first name to World, and aimed it at the melodic, positive hardcore they grew up on.

eras.title: Named for World B. Free
eras.text: Scott Vogel of Terror, Andrew Kline of Strife, Joe Garlipp of Despair and Sammy Siegler of Judge wanted to make something more melodic and positive than their other bands. The name came off an NBA roster.

years.h: World Be Free take their name from Lloyd "World B." Free
years.p: The band is named for NBA guard Lloyd Free, who changed his name to World B. Free in 1981. His line about saying what he'll do, then doing it, becomes the band's motto.

years.h: Arthur Smilios of Gorilla Biscuits joins on bass
years.p: Bassist [[Arthur Smilios|40d4f905-3bb1-4d2e-9a9b-1d7891033094]], of [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and [[CIV|1649c891-eea0-45b2-8caf-c85d985ff3bd]], rounds out World Be Free, and [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] guests on the song I'm Done.

eras.title: One drummer, two bands a night
eras.text: The debut album came out on Revelation and the band went straight out on tour, half of it opening for Judge. That meant Sammy Siegler playing two sets a night.

years.p: Recorded on a small budget at Hurley Studios on vintage Neve gear, with Scott Vogel's vocals done at Terror drummer Nick Jett's studio in Granada Hills.

years.h: World Be Free's first tour, with Judge on the East Coast
years.p: Starting at San Diego's Che Cafe and a Fullerton skate shop, then Buffalo, Philadelphia and Cambridge opening for Judge, with Sammy Siegler drumming for both. It ends at St. Vitus in Brooklyn.

years.h: Full set filmed by hate5six, February 19, 2016
yt: Full set filmed by hate5six, February 19, 2016

eras.title: One time for unity
eras.text: The band went quiet after the first album, lost its bassist to the other coast, and came back four years later with a Chain of Strength member and a more melodic EP.

years.h: Alex Barreto of Chain of Strength replaces Arthur Smilios
years.p: Smilios leaves World Be Free because of his job and life on the East Coast. [[Alex Barreto|9e81a640-5c20-444e-9064-d2d65cf87328]] of [[Chain of Strength|81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8]] and [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]] takes over bass.

q: The band was kinda 'dead' for lack of a better term.
years.h: "Acceptance" premieres, and World Be Free are back
years.p: Decibel premieres Acceptance, the first new World Be Free song since 2016. Scott Vogel admits the band had gone dormant before it.

Five songs picked from about fifteen written. [[Chuck Ragan|97417292-3fb0-40ea-8837-5540cfb4de71]] of [[Hot Water Music|c83907ee-8b5a-4547-8f68-96572243ea7f]] sings on the title track, and Andrew Kline calls Down & Beyond World Be Free gone prog.
